fatal_errors: The proposed CrN or TiN films do not reconstruct the target FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy-alloy coating.
None of the cited evidence supports adhesion or wear performance of CrN or TiN coatings on Cu.
The hypothesis omits the temperature-dependent transition near 900 K and its lattice-disorder/dislocation mechanism.
explanation: The response is only broadly aligned with surface protection of Cu and offers a basic coated-versus-uncoated falsification test. It fails to identify the target material, coating geometry, FCC structure, nanoindentation/friction protocol, or temperature range. Its generic claim of improved wear resistance does not capture the stable behavior through 600 K, sharp degradation at and above 900 K, or increasing friction. The cited papers discuss high-entropy alloys and their general properties, not CrN/TiN-on-Cu adhesion, so they do not validate the proposed material or mechanism.
